title: Frontend: Find the Single Element in a Sorted Array
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Find the Single Element in a Sorted Array. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution(values). A sorted odd-length nonempty array contains one singleton and pairs of every other value. Return the singleton in logarithmic time.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Use binary search and align the midpoint to an even index.
alternativeApproaches: Explain why the parity invariant fails if counts are not exactly two or the array is not sorted.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Singleton first/last; one-element array; ordinary middle.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
